gold_option: Large middle cerebral artery territory embolic stroke
gold_diagnosis: Large middle cerebral artery territory embolic stroke

options.B: Large vessel occlusion stroke (middle cerebral artery atherosclerosis)
options.C: Acute ischemic stroke (cardioembolic origin secondary to atrial fibrillation)
options.D: Large middle cerebral artery territory embolic stroke

A.rationale: Pacemaker lead-associated thromboembolic stroke is a specific type of stroke that matches the leaf label exactly.

B.rationale: Large vessel occlusion stroke (middle cerebral artery atherosclerosis) does not match any leaf label directly.

C.rationale: Acute ischemic stroke (cardioembolic origin secondary to atrial fibrillation) is equivalent to cardioembolic stroke.

D.rationale: Large middle cerebral artery territory embolic stroke is a subtype of cardioembolic stroke.

vignette_preview:
A man in his 70s presented to the emergency department with left-sided hemiparesis, dysarthria, gaze deviation in his right eye, and left-sided hemineglect. His medical history was significant for permanent atrial fibrillation and complete heart block for which he had a pacemaker implanted in the late 1990s that was subsequently upgraded to a biventricular system.

Blood pressure was 147/75 mm Hg, heart rate was 84 beats per minute, respiratory rate was 16 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation was 99% on room air.

- Imaging Studies:    Computed tomography angiography was consistent with a large middle cerebral artery territory.      - Electrocardiogram Findings:    Shows a ventricular-paced rhythm with ventricular bigeminy at an overall mean rate of 84 beats per minute. Two pacing stimuli visible, best seen in lead II. The first of each bigeminal complex is initiated by a pacemaker stimulus resulting in ventricular depolarization. Each paced QRS complex is followed by a premature ventricular complex (PVC), with a second pacemaker stimulus occurring about 60 msec after onset of the PVC.        Image Title: Figure 1. Electrocardiogram on Presentation to the Emergency Department
